newsitem.title: UK: S&P sets criteria for UK property securitisations.
newsitem.headline: S&P sets criteria for UK property securitisations.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had introduced criteria for rating securitisations backed by commercial real estate properties in the UK.

"Despite a commercial real estate market in the UK of 300 billion stg, the direct involvement via securitisation could bring a number of benefits, including diversified funding and the ability for the originator to retain the upside potential in the securitised portfolio," S&P said in a statement.
S&P compared the potential involvement to the U.S. where capital market funding had gone from nothing to 10 percent in five years.
"S&P has been rating commercial real estate securitisations in the U.S. for many years, but its UK criteria reflect the unique features of that market," the agency said.
S&P said the criteria covered all aspects of its analysis, including credit and cash flow analysis, due diligence requirements, surveillance and legal considerations.

"The credit analysis is fundamentally a property analysis focusing on location, quality of product and specification, but because of the unique characteristics of the UK market, credit is also given to the cash flows received from tenants in the portfolio," said S&P.
